Public beta · free

Install Teachie Beachie on your FM‑1

Thirty lessons that teach the FM‑1, on the FM‑1 itself.

Teachie Beachie teaches kids, and any beginner, to make music on the M‑VAVE FM‑1. You don't need to read music or open a manual: every lesson shows you what to press, right on the FM‑1's screen.A lesson puts a short card on the screen, lights up the button or key to press, and waits while you try it. If you get stuck it offers a hint, and it can even do the step for you. Each lesson takes a few minutes and builds on the one before.There are thirty lessons in four parts: Your first beat, Notes and chords, Effects and sound, Make a song. By lesson 7 you have made a beat of your own. By lesson 30, a whole song.Teachie Beachie is free, and once it is installed no computer is needed. It is built on SLOOP 3, a complete groovebox, which stays when the lessons are done.I made Teachie Beachie for my kids, nieces and nephews, as part of a Christmas present. If you have kids who would like to learn how to use a groovebox and the FM‑1, I'd encourage you to give Teachie Beachie a try.

  • About 10 minutes the first time, 1 minute to update
  • A full backup before anything is written
  • Nothing to install on your computer

Take it further with an AI assistant

The lessons are plain text files, written to be read by people and by AI. Open this project on a computer, in an AI assistant that works with files, and you have a tutor for the learner, a lesson writer for you, and a second pair of hands on the FM‑1. Teachie Beachie was built and tested this way.

Ask about any step

The assistant knows every lesson: each step, its hints, and what usually goes wrong. Ask it what a step wants, or have it explain an idea another way.

Control the FM‑1

With the FM‑1 plugged in, the assistant can work it: load a lesson's song, press play, change the tempo, write notes, light up a button. It can show a move, or set up a practice round.

Change a lesson

Tell it a card is confusing. It rewrites the card, checks that the words fit the FM‑1's screen, tests the lesson on a simulated FM‑1, and sends it to yours.

Write your own

A new lesson for a kid who wants more drums, or an easier one. The assistant writes it, tests it the same way, and adds it to the FM‑1.

How to set it up, and what to ask. Any assistant that can read files and run commands will do.

Step 1 of 6

Before you start

Teachie Beachie is new. Here is what to expect, and what you need.

Teachie Beachie runs SLOOP 3, a public betaSLOOP 3 is new and still being tested on real FM-1s, and so is Teachie Beachie, so you may meet bugs. This page backs up your FM-1 before it changes anything, so you can always go back. When something goes wrong, tell us: every report makes it better.
Tested on the original flash chip onlyTeachie Beachie has been tested on my FM‑1, which has the original flash chip. FM‑1s sold since fall 2026 can have a newer chip, the UCUN UC25HQ80, and neither Teachie Beachie nor SLOOP 3 has been tried on one yet. If yours is one of them, you would be among the first.

You need

  • An M-VAVE FM-1 and a USB data cable (a charge-only cable won't work), plugged straight into the computer.
  • Chrome or Edge on Windows, macOS, Linux or ChromeOS (or Chrome on Android).
  • The FM-1 powered by USB the whole time.
Already use SLOOP?
Prefer the tried and tested version?SLOOP 2.8 stays available on its own page: isod89.github.io/sloop-fm1. Teachie Beachie never changes SLOOP 2.8's data, so you can go back at any time with your backup.
Updating from SLOOP 3.0 to 3.3.4?Since 3.3.5 the FM-1 keeps one project, with room for the fullest one. At the first start, the newest of your 8 projects is kept. Before you install: open the web editor, Projects, BACK UP EVERYTHING. The editor puts any of them back later.
Teachie Beachie already on your FM-1?To get this page's lessons without installing again, send the lessons only.
The whole install: about 10 minutes the first time.
Step 2 of 6

The safety net: m-bootloader

Teachie Beachie installs through m-bootloader, a small free program that sits under the firmware. If an install is ever interrupted, your FM-1 opens a recovery menu instead of getting stuck. You set it up once.

Is it already there? Check in 10 seconds

  1. Switch the FM-1 off.
  2. Hold PLAY and switch it on. Keep holding about a second.
  3. A menu with BOOT APP, DOWNLOAD MODE and MIDI MODE? Then it's there.
Recommended · Windows, macOS, Linux

With M-Flasher

M-Flasher ↗m-bootloader (fm1-uboot.boot) ↗
  1. Download M-Flasher and fm1-uboot.boot (links above). Windows: run M-Flasher.exe as administrator (it isn't signed: More info → Run anyway). macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.
  2. Connect the FM-1 and click DOWNLOAD MODE in M-Flasher (or, with SLOOP 2.8 running, hold OCT- and OCT+ for 5 seconds). The screen doesn't change; the computer sees a disk named WL82 UBOOT1.00. If Windows offers to format it, click Cancel.
  3. Back up the whole FM-1 with M-Flasher and keep the file: it brings your FM-1 back exactly as it is today.
  4. Install the bootloader with fm1-uboot.boot. Only the boot area is written: your current firmware stays.
  5. Switch the FM-1 off and on while holding PLAY: the menu appears.
Alternative · FM-1 on M-VAVE's own firmware

With M-VAVE's M-UPGRADE app

Download fm1-uboot.fwsc from the latest m-bootloader release, open it in M-UPGRADE (close other MIDI apps first) and start the upgrade. It writes only the bootloader. If in doubt, prefer M-Flasher, which also makes the full backup.

Good to know
  • Keep the power on while the bootloader is written.
  • FM-1s sold since fall 2026 have another flash chip, the UCUN UC25HQ80 (JEDEC 0xB36014). m-bootloader has not been run on it yet, and one such unit did not start after it was installed. Use M-Flasher 0.9.1 or newer, which warns you, and make its backup first. Teachie Beachie accepts this chip, but it has not been tried on one yet either.
  • M-VAVE's official updates put their own bootloader back: after one, do this step again.
Step 3 of 6

Connect your FM-1

Start the FM-1 in MIDI MODE, plug it in, and let this page find it.

  1. Switch the FM-1 off, then on while holding PLAY.
  2. In the menu, choose MIDI MODE with OCT- / OCT+, then press PLAY. The screen asks you to connect USB.
  3. Plug it into the computer with the USB cable, then click Connect. When the browser asks to control your MIDI devices, click Allow.
Looking for your FM-1…
Keep it in MIDI MODE and plugged in. It's found automatically as soon as it appears.
FM-1 connected

Coming from SLOOP 2.8?Teachie Beachie does not open the project SLOOP 2.8 left (SLOOP 3 does; Teachie Beachie leaves that out to make room for its lessons). Your presets, favorites, samples, SYN kits, FM6 bank and settings come along. SLOOP 2.8's data is only read, never written.
Technical details

Help

The answers to what can go wrong. Still stuck? Ask in the issues.

“No FM-1 found”
Check that the FM-1 shows MIDI MODE (step 3), and that the cable carries data: try another cable or USB port, without a hub. Close other apps that use MIDI (M-UPGRADE, editors, music software), then click Connect again.
“The FM-1 is running a firmware”
It started SLOOP, or another firmware, instead of the menu. Switch it off, then on while holding PLAY about a second. If no menu appears, m-bootloader isn't installed yet (step 2).
The install stopped halfway
Nothing is lost. Nothing is erased before the whole package has been checked. If it stops while writing, m-bootloader sees an incomplete firmware at the next start and opens its menu by itself: reload this page and install again.
The browser never asks about MIDI
Use Chrome or Edge. Click the icon left of the address, open the site settings, and allow MIDI devices. Then reload the page.
The backup stops
Some m-bootloader versions don't answer reads. Make the backup with M-Flasher instead (step 2), then tick “I already have a full backup”.
Teachie Beachie doesn't start, or starts badly
Hold OCT- while switching on: RESCUE. PLAY starts with an empty project (your saved project is kept). Or hold PLAY for m-bootloader's menu and install again. Then tell us what the screen showed.
Going back to SLOOP 2.8 or M-VAVE's firmware
Restore your backup with M-Flasher (hold REC while switching on for download mode). It brings the FM-1 back exactly as it was when you made it. Projects made with Teachie Beachie since then are not in it: save them as files with the web editor first.
Updating Teachie Beachie later
Open this page again: steps 3 to 5, about a minute. Your project and your sounds stay.

The stable version, SLOOP 2.8: github.com/isod89/sloop-fm1.
